value: Monday morning: flights are near normal, with no ground stops on the FAA status feed at 10:16 AM ET. FlightAware counts about 18,100 US cancellations Friday through Sunday. The FAA's written Q&A traces the Nov. 13 data flood to a new router at an El Dorado, Ark., radio site and a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, both on the L3Harris-run FTI network. Duffy says the Amarillo router, replaced about three weeks earlier, began flooding when the El Dorado router came on. Both routers are in L3Harris's Florida lab with FAA, Juniper and Cisco engineers; the root cause is still not determined. Router maker HPE says the device worked as the installer configured it (Reported). The FAA says it has no indication of a cyberattack. FAA/DOT staff brief House T&I today on the $30.1 billion request ($10.1 billion for ATC); no hearing date is posted. The ask has grown to up to $50 billion, and government funding runs out Dec. 11.

Latest (Wed 8:18 AM ET): DOT's written release quotes Duffy saying investigators have recreated the El Dorado overload in the L3Harris lab but still lack a root cause (Confirmed). Three new Reported threads point at process, not just hardware: the Washington Post says an FAA official supervised and signed off on the El Dorado work minutes before the network faltered; KATV reports a 2025 FAA procedure change that auto-approves contractor upgrades; and a CRN source says the device's broadcast/multicast feature should have been off. All single-source. Still no written root cause, FBI or CISA finding, IG or NTSB review, or hearing date. Latest (Tue 5:16 PM ET): The administration formally asked appropriators for $50.1 billion (DOT release; $10.1 billion for ATC technology including more resilient telecom), and Duffy and Bedford pitched it at the Senate GOP lunch, where Thune, Cruz, Kennedy and Capito voiced doubts about the size. The Senate Commerce Democrats' Juniper-pause letter is now posted (Confirmed), with answers due Nov. 23. The FBI says its Cyber teams are providing technical assistance and have not taken any equipment. Still no written root cause, FBI or CISA finding, IG or NTSB review, hearing date, or House staff briefing readout. Latest (Mon 5:14 PM ET): Duffy said on CNBC the root cause is still unclear and that FBI agents are at the L3Harris lab with FAA staff (Reuters, Bloomberg; Reported). The House T&I staff briefing is reported moved to Tuesday, when Duffy is also expected at the Senate GOP lunch. Still no written root cause, FBI or CISA finding, IG or NTSB review, or hearing date. Mon 10:25 AM ET: Officials' account is now in writing (FAA Q&A) but the root cause isn't: it's faulty router vs. installation/configuration, and why two sites flooded together. HPE's statement leans toward configuration, and PASS says FAA technicians weren't involved. Both are interested parties, so treat them as claims. No FBI or CISA finding has been published. The WSJ's Indianapolis-first detail and POLITICO's memo are still single-source. Operations are back to near normal. Watch today's staff briefing and any hearing date. Earlier: The national ground stop was cancelled at 8:16 PM ET (Advisory 005), all at once, and by 1:27 AM ET Saturday the last airline-requested hub stop was gone; the FAA summary lists no ground stops. At the White House briefing (~8:35 PM ET), officials gave a cause on the record, reported by Reuters, BBC, the LA Times and Aviation Week: Duffy said legacy analog TDM switches and routers carrying ATC voice and radar data were overloaded with data and began giving inconsistent data at 3:36 PM ET, so the FAA shut the system down; radar and communications were never fully lost. Mullin said new equipment being added was overwhelming the older system, that there is "zero evidence" so far of a cyberattack or rogue AI though neither is ruled out, that it "appears this was mechanically driven," and that the NSA is assisting DHS. AvWeb quotes Duffy saying SMART is not connected to STARS or ERAM and that "There's no possible way SMART would have impacted what happened"; a SMART role stays unconfirmed because Reuters has Mullin saying a rogue AI is not fully ruled out. No official transcript or written FAA report is posted, and the FAA newsroom still says only "communication issues." Saturday at the 10:30 AM ET DOT briefing, Duffy named the trigger on the record: L3Harris copper-to-fiber work at a remote FAA site, with a router involved in the work flooding the network (Yahoo News; AInvest). Still not named: the specific site; not determined: whether the router was faulty or the contractor erred. Reuters, citing two airline officials, says the affected network is the L3Harris-overseen one; L3Harris has not commented. A Saturday Hindustan Times explainer, citing Bloomberg, says some equipment was already running over capacity and that L3Harris has been asked to diagnose the overload; those details stay Reported/unconfirmed. CBS (an update caused a reboot and crash) and Bloomberg (the FBI is looking at a software update) also remain sourced reports, not confirmed. The Air Current, citing airline sources, reports the outage was first noticed at Chicago Center, then Boston, Washington, New York and Minneapolis in rapid succession — reported, not an official log. A circulating claim that NWS/NEXRAD weather radar went down nationwide is debunked; a few airport terminal Doppler radars had brief dropouts, and FAA ATC radar data was intermittent because it rides the overloaded telecom network. On funding: $12.5 billion was already approved in July 2025; Duffy and Vought renewed a $30.1 billion request Friday morning (about $10.1 billion ATC tech, $2 billion towers, $18 billion airports) and Duffy raised the public ask to $50 billion after the outage. House T&I will "thoroughly review" the stop; Sen. Cantwell, Sen. Duckworth and Rep. Lieu have pressed for answers or hearings; no hearing date, NTSB or Inspector General review has been announced. Saturday morning, Duffy said it is safe to fly; the 10:30 AM ET briefing with FAA Administrator Bedford took place, and coverage so far reports no NTSB/IG review, hearing date, center-by-center detail or new SMART statement.
